paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. The word *secured* refers to the cash: in a cash account the broker holds the full purchase price as collateral for the whole life of the trade [S1].

**Assignment** is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised [S2]. When a put holder exercises, some put writer is obliged to take the shares at the strike [S2]. The Options Clearing Corporation assigns exercise notices at random to clearing members with short positions in the same series [S2].

The good-to-own quality gate is a **filter, not a discovery engine**: it decides which tickers are allowed into the option screeners at all, records a reason for every rejection, and produces a score for the survivors [S5].

**LEAPS** (Long-term Equity AnticiPation Securities) is the exchanges' name for listed options with more than a year until expiration [S3]. They trade and settle exactly like shorter options; only the time horizon is different [S3].

The screen is a {{ regime.label }} regime with a VIX of {{ regime.vix }} at the {{ regime.vix_percentile|percent }} percentile and a risk-free rate of {{ regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct }}.
